newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Police arrest 'cocaine granny' in Brazil.
newsitem.headline: Police arrest 'cocaine granny' in Brazil.

text.p: A 63-year-old Brazilian woman who earned the nickname "cocaine granny" for allegedly running one of Rio de Janeiro state's biggest cocaine distribution networks was arrested thanks to an anonymous tip to authorities, police said Sunday.

Maria Helena Gomes and her son Luiz Carlos Gomes were arrested on Friday when they tried to withdraw money from a bank in Pontapora, a city in the central state of Matto Grosso about 1,000 miles (1,800 km) northwest of Sao Paulo.
Police said an anonymous caller told authorities that Gomes and her son had recently opened an account at the bank. Police were staking out the bank when Gomes and Luiz showed up on Friday.
The Brazilian press nicknamed Gomes "cocaine granny" four years ago when she assumed control of Luiz's cocaine wholesaling operation after his arrest.
News reports said Gomes was supplying up to 180 pounds (80 kg) of pure cocaine every 15 days to 200 sites in Rio de Janeiro state, including several in Niteroi, a large suburb of Rio de Janeiro.
Luiz joined up with his mother after his release from prison last year and the two began operating out of Pontapora, news reports said.
